newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Eletrobras to sell Light shrs.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Eletrobras to sell Light shrs.

text.p: Brazil's government said it plans to sell 28.8 percent of state power firm Eletrobras' 34.79 percent stake in Light electricity company on local and foreign markets in the second half of 1997.
Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) expects to release in the next three weeks the names of financial institutions that will manage the sale of the shares, a BNDES spokeswoman said.
Among those competing to act as sale manager are Merrill Lynch, Robert Fleming, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Salomon Brothers and ABN Amro Bank, she said.
Light, which was privatized in May, is owned by a group comprised of France's EDF, U.S. firms Houston Industries and AES Corp, Brazilian steel mill CSN and BNDES's investment arm.
The group owns 54.67 percent of Light's capital stock. Eletrobras and minority shareholders hold the rest.
